chalisa.do1: Victory, victory to Tulasī, the Goddess, the truthful one, the giver of joy. Salutations, salutations to Śrī Vṛndā, the beloved of Hari, a mine of virtues.
chalisa.do2: Mother, you who are seated on Śrī Hari's head, grant an undying boon. Vṛndāvanī, for the good of your people, delay no longer.
chalisa.cau1: Blessed, blessed is Śrī Tulasī, the Mother; the Vedas ever sing her unfathomable glory. ॥1॥
chalisa.cau2: You are dearer to Hari than his very life; for Hari alone you performed great austerities. ॥2॥
chalisa.cau3: When Hari, well pleased, appeared before you, you joined your hands and made this prayer to him: ॥3॥
chalisa.cau4: Lord, be my husband; knowing me humble, do not withdraw your affection. ॥4॥
chalisa.cau5: Lakṣmī heard Tulasī's words and, growing angry, laid a curse on her: ॥5॥
chalisa.cau6: You who ask for that unfitting boon, become a tree, and bear an insentient body. ॥6॥
chalisa.cau7: Hearing this, Tulasī in turn cursed her on that spot: You too shall dwell in the homes of the lowly. ॥7॥
chalisa.cau8: Then Hari at once gave his word: Listen, fair-faced one, do not be distressed. ॥8॥
chalisa.cau9: In time I shall be your husband; your hope will be fulfilled, my word is true. ॥9॥
chalisa.cau10: Then in Gokula there was a cowherd, Sudāmā; Tulasī, you became his wife. ॥10॥
chalisa.cau11: In Śrī Kṛṣṇa's rāsa dance, Rādhā could not bear to see that love. ॥11॥
chalisa.cau12: She at once cursed Tulasī: Girl, be born in the world of men. ॥12॥
chalisa.cau13: That cowherd became the demon king named Śaṅkhacūḍa, the crown of all. ॥13॥
chalisa.cau14: Tulasī became his wife, supremely chaste, a store of virtue and beauty. ॥14॥
chalisa.cau15: When two aeons had passed in this way, then in the third aeon she was born. ॥15॥
chalisa.cau16: Tulasī's name became Vṛndā, and her husband's name was Jalandhara, a demon. ॥16॥
chalisa.cau17: Waging fierce combat, that abode of matchless strength did battle with Śiva. ॥17॥
chalisa.cau18: When Śiva was defeated with his army and the demon did not die, then Śiva called on Hari. ॥18॥
chalisa.cau19: Vṛndā was a wife devoted to her husband, and no one could slay him. ॥19॥
chalisa.cau20: Then Hari took the very guise of Jalandhara and went to Vṛndā. ॥20॥
chalisa.cau21: For Śiva's sake, contriving a deception, he broke your sacred chastity. ॥21॥
chalisa.cau22: Jalandhara was slain; hearing it, her heart was torn up by grief. ॥22॥
chalisa.cau23: At that moment Hari put aside his deception; Vṛndā saw, and in sorrow uttered these words: ॥23॥
chalisa.cau24: As you slew the fearless Jalandhara, so that same one, as Rāvaṇa, will carry off Sītā. ॥24॥
chalisa.cau25: Such is your heart, like stone, that you broke dharma and slew my husband. ॥25॥
chalisa.cau26: For this reason, take my curse: may your body become stone. ॥26॥
chalisa.cau27: Hearing this, Hari at once spoke these words: You have cursed without thinking. ॥27॥
chalisa.cau28: You did not see your husband's own deeds, when he sought to deceive Pārvatī. ॥28॥
chalisa.cau29: Dull-minded one, you too shall be of such an insentient form: the peerless tulasī tree in the world. ॥29॥
chalisa.cau30: I shall take the form of the śālagrāma, lovely in the midst of the river Gaṇḍakī. ॥30॥
chalisa.cau31: Those who offer me tulasī leaves will enjoy every happiness and attain the supreme state. ॥31॥
chalisa.cau32: Without tulasī Hari's body burns, and great pain rises in his head and heart. ॥32॥
chalisa.cau33: Whoever places tulasī leaves on Hari's head pours out a thousand pitchers of nectar. ॥33॥
chalisa.cau34: Tulasī delights Hari's heart and destroys disease, fault and sorrow. ॥34॥
chalisa.cau35: In ceaseless, loving worship of Hari there is no difference between Tulasī and Rādhā. ॥35॥
chalisa.cau36: Though there be dishes of fifty-six kinds, without tulasī leaves they are not dear to Hari. ॥36॥
chalisa.cau37: All the holy places are in the shade of the tulasī tree; there people gain liberation, without doubt. ॥37॥
chalisa.cau38: Sundara, a poet, sings Hari's praises; singing near Tulasī, he gains a thousandfold fruit. ॥38॥
chalisa.cau39: He lives near Durvāsā's abode, a lovely place to the east of Prayāga. ॥39॥
chalisa.cau40: Men and women who recite this daily become happy: so says Śiva, the foe of Tripura. ॥40॥
chalisa.do3: The woman who reads the Tulasī Chālīsā, keeps a tulasī plant in her home and offers lamps gains a son as its fruit, even if she is childless.
chalisa.do4: Supremely pleased, Hari takes away all sorrow and poverty; blessings, wealth and family are gained, and the home here dwells full.
chalisa.do5: One gains in the world the fruit one desires, and all one's wishes are fulfilled; where tulasī leaves are offered, there Hari dwells a thousandfold.
chalisa.do6: Seeing the glory and the name of Tulasī, Sukharāma, son of Tulasī, Tulasīdāsa, composed this Mānasa Chālīsā in the world.
